inputCoverage.osmSnapshot: 2026-08-11 Protomaps z14; 6×6 tile window before our conflation
inputCoverage.agencyScope: Complete features intersecting input window from existing source cache; not a fresh agency census

recommendation.summary: There is substantial overlap, but neither source has a decisive geometric quality advantage. Inspect the shared bends and endpoints before choosing.
reasons: OpenStreetMap: 90% of its geometry lies within 15 m of the other source; 100% within 50 m. Median nearest-line offset 1.2 m.
USFS: 92% of its geometry lies within 15 m of the other source; 100% within 50 m. Median nearest-line offset 1.1 m.

Within the same input window, OpenStreetMap: 4,317 m long, median vertex spacing 12.5 m, 0 m outside the other source’s 50 m corridor; USFS: 4,016 m long, median vertex spacing 19.7 m, 0 m outside the other source’s 50 m corridor.

Endpoint check: OpenStreetMap has 0 non-seam endpoint candidates over 75 m from the other alignment; USFS has 0 non-seam endpoint candidates over 75 m from the other alignment. These can be real additions, branches, or source gaps; inspect their connections.

DEM sanity check in the shared corridor: OpenStreetMap: 90th-percentile absolute terrain grade 24.8% over 76 sampled 50 m sections; USFS: 90th-percentile absolute terrain grade 25.8% over 78 sampled 50 m sections. Lower grade alone does not mean a route is more accurate.
Vertex density measures representation detail, not survey accuracy. Sharp turns may be genuine switchbacks; geometry alone cannot diagnose GPS multipath.
recommendation.limitations: Heuristic guidance, not an independent ground-truth verdict. Uses source geometry and frozen DEM only; no imagery interpretation or route editing. DEM measures ground surface, not surveyed trail elevation. Full agency inputs and OSM tile fragments have different lineage; no automatic edits.
